name: MetaEval
description: Benchmarks serve as standardized test systems to distinguish capabilities among large language models (LLMs). Discriminative items enable high-ability LLMs to favor correct answers, while causing low-ability models to assign lower plausibility to these answers and tend toward incorrect answers. Current methods for assessing benchmark quality primarily focus on coverage of difficulty levels and task diversity, yet lack direct quantification of discrimination—the core metric. Furthermore, large-scale benchmarks incur high evaluation costs.
